row.entry: US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Satellite Networked Open Ground Station, a network of volunteer ground stations
Secure Shell, used to log in to the server from another computer
Two-line element set, the standard format for a satellite's orbit
Record that an operator has seen an alert. The alert stays in the list until its condition clears.
The higher alert severity. A value is outside its alarm limits, or a condition needs attention now.
The signed record of every operator action. Each entry carries a fingerprint (hash) of the one before it.
The short identifier, usually initials, that signs every action you take.
The lower alert severity. A value is outside its caution limits, or a condition may need attention.
One telemetry value, such as a battery voltage or temperature.
A channel moving away from its learned normal for the same point in the orbit, even while inside its limits.
The part of each orbit in Earth's shadow.
An alert about something that happened once, such as a restart, rather than a condition that continues.
One run of the job that collects new frames from SatNOGS, every 30 minutes by default.
One packet of telemetry received by a ground station.
The signed transfer of the console from one operator to the next.
Hide an alert for a set time, with a reason. Shelving is signed in the audit trail.
No new decoded frames for longer than the stale period, 12 hours by default.
